The product photos are owned by Takara Tomy / Hasbro and the wiki uploads by Fandom contributors; use for personal reference only. image_confidence: high = image is labeled as this exact part (e.g. File:BladeWizardRod.png); medium = combo/set/packaging shot that contains the part, or a same-mold variant page image; null = no image found. Gathered 2026-11-06 via the fandom MediaWiki API. Hotlink protection: static.wikia.nocookie.net returns 404 when a request carries a non-Fandom Referer header (verified 2026-11-06), so when embedding these in a page use (or a ); direct requests without a Referer return the image.

user_name_check.Gear Ball: EXISTS. Bit Gear Ball (GB), stamina (BX-24 / G0198).
user_name_check.Free Flat: EXISTS. Bit Free Flat (FF), attack, new in 2026 (BX-49 DranStrike 4-50FF / G2742 Strike Dran).
user_name_check.Free Ball: EXISTS. Bit Free Ball (FB), stamina (UX-08 SilverWolf 3-80FB / G1674 Sterling Wolf).

user_name_check.Pop Out: NO bit is officially named "Pop Out". Most likely the Turbo (Tr) ratchet-integrated bit from Pegasus Blast ATr, whose sharp tip pops out while spinning fast and retracts later. The user owns Pegasus Blast, which makes this more likely. Less likely alternatives: Bound Spike (spring-loaded tip that sinks), Operate (twist mode switch), Elevate. Confirm with the user.

notes: NAMING: Takara Tomy (TT) writes names as one word ("WizardRod"). Hasbro usually reverses the word order ("Wand Wizard", "Sword Dran", "Courage Dran") and renames some parts: Hells->Incendio, Valkyrie->Valkerion, Brave->Courage, Eclipse->Umbra, Fortress->Armor, Bucks->Stag, Antlers->Antler, StormSpriggan->Storm Spryzen, XenoXcalibur->Xeno Xcalius, HeavensRing->Ring Aether, SiegSuperion->Suppress Superion, BulletGriffon->Rocket Griffon, GloryValkyrie->Glory Valkerion, HellsNether->Nether Incendio, TriceraPress->Brace Triceratops, TriceraSpiky->Ridge Triceratops. "name" uses the TT name with spaces when TT sells it, otherwise the Hasbro name. alt_names lists the rest. Match user input against both.

LINES: BX = Basic Line; UX = Unique Line (more metal on the outer rim); CX = Custom Line (multi-piece blade). "Expand" (Infinity) sub-lines arrived in 2026: BX Expand (metal joined through the centre: DranStrike, HeavensRing, LusterDragoon, SiegSuperion, Hasbro CyclopsEye/Glare Cyclops, Shatter Horus); UX Expand = ratchet-integrated blades; CX Expand = 4-piece blades.

MULTI-PIECE (CX, from March 2025): blade = Lock Chip + Main Blade + Assist Blade, then ratchet + bit. Combo code e.g. DranBrave S6-60V = Dran lock chip, Brave main blade, Slash (S) assist, 6-60 ratchet, Vortex (V) bit. Hasbro writes "Courage Dran S 6-60V".

CX EXPAND (from 2026-03, CX-13+): 4-piece blade = Lock Chip + Over Blade + Metal Blade + Assist Blade (no Main Blade). Code letters are Over + Assist, e.g. BahamutBlitz BK1-50I = Bahamut chip, Break (B) over blade, Blitz metal blade, Knuckle (K) assist, 1-50 ratchet, Ignition bit. Per fandom wiki, Over/Metal blades are not meant to be mixed with standard Main Blades. Check that before allowing cross-system builds.

Lock chips, main/over/metal/assist blades are listed separately under cx_parts so the app can build custom CX blades. Blades with line "CX" in blades[] are the officially named combos, each with its components.

BUILT-IN RATCHETS: (1) Ratchet-Integrated Blades (UX Expand, 2026): BulletGriffon/Rocket Griffon, GloryValkyrie/Glory Valkerion, HellsNether/Nether Incendio, plus Hasbro-original Cutter Shinobi, Rampart Aegis, Seize Jaguar, Valor Bison. Combos are blade + bit only (e.g. "Rocket Griffon H"). (2) Ratchet-Integrated Bits: Turbo (Tr, Pegasus Blast ATr) and Operate (Op, Emperor Might HOp). They replace both ratchet and bit, so the combo has no ratchet number. Deck validation must allow a missing ratchet in both cases.

COLLABS: Hasbro-led Marvel / Star Wars / Transformers / Jurassic World multipacks are Basic Line blades with character gear chips. Several reuse existing molds (Red Hulk = TyrannoBeat retool, T. Rex = TyrannoBeat, Mosasaurus = TriceraSpiky, Spinosaurus = TyrannoRoar, Quetzalcoatlus = PteraSwing, Snowtrooper = Stormtrooper). TT also sold most of them as BX-00 multipacks. TT-side collabs: Evangelion Deck Set (Eva lock chip, CX), Ultraman TigaRage (CX), plus FC Barcelona / J.League / Giants / Japan national team colourways (recolours only, not new parts).

Hasbro-only parts (no TT retail equivalent found): Clamp Crab, Yell Kong, Hack Viking, Stun Medusa, Gust Bat, Shatter Horus, Glare Cyclops (TT dev name CyclopsEye), Cutter Shinobi, Rampart Aegis, Seize Jaguar, Valor Bison, Hurricane Enlil (Enlil lock chip, I over blade, Hurricane metal blade), AFC/NFC lock chips.

TT-only so far (no Hasbro release found): Aero Pegasus, Lightning L-Drago (2 types), Xeno Xcalibur (Hasbro name "Xeno Xcalius" listed on wiki but no product code), Storm Spriggan, Luster Dragoon, Sol Eclipse, Wolf Hunt, Phoenix Flare, Valkyrie Volt, Drake Brave, Tiga Rage, Eva blades.

UPCOMING / NOT YET ON SALE as of 2026-11-06: CX-20 Customize Set C (2026-11-21): Phoenix Force WHM-65MT, Weight over blade, Force metal blade, M-65 ratchet, Metal Taper bit. BX-54 SiegSuperion 0-70LP (2026-11-21 in Japan; Hasbro Suppress Superion G2745 reportedly August 2026, so Low Point may already be out via Hasbro). Several 2026 Hasbro codes have no confirmed date on the wiki: G2736, G2737, G2745, G2752, G2758-G2763, G3064, G3497, G3745, G3797, G4564-G4566, G4569, G4570. Those entries are marked medium confidence.
Disk Ball vs Disc Ball: TT/wiki spelling is "Disk Ball" (DB). Retailers often write "Disc Ball". Same part. Disk Spike (DS, 2026) is a separate part.
Fused ratchet+bit and integrated blades break the usual blade/ratchet/bit three-slot model. Mark them in the app.

Data method: part list and infobox fields (type, spin, first product codes) come from the Beyblade fandom wiki API; release dates and descriptions were checked against the official Takara Tomy lineup pages; Hasbro codes come from the wiki Hasbro product list and retailer listings. product_codes lists the debut code first, then other products that include the part. BX-00/UX-00/CX-00 are TT limited/promo codes.

Not verified / gaps: Trypio has a wiki page but no product. Kid lock chip / KidHunt K4-70TK is not on the official TT site. Dran Arc S2-70K is fandom-only. Tiga Rage component split is inferred. AFC/NFC main and assist blades are unknown. Types for some remix CX combos and Eva blades are unknown. Hasbro full names for Sol Eclipse / Emperor Might are unverified. Type labels follow the wiki and can disagree with retailers (e.g. Disk Spike is called defense in the infobox and stamina in its text).
